dashboard.title: About the Overview section
dashboard.lead: Your home screen after signing in. A summary of activity across your tests, recent respondent activity and quick shortcuts to in-progress drafts. Nothing is configured here — it's a view.

what_you_configure.heading: What you see here
items: Summary metrics: number of active tests, sessions, respondents and completion rate
Your latest test with respondent activity over the last 7 days
In-progress drafts (max 3) with a "Continue editing" button
Optional cards: weekly digest, course recommendations, retest reminders (rolled out gradually)

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Metrics load when the page opens; refresh for fresh data
"Recent activity" cards update within seconds of a respondent finishing a session
Weekly summaries are compiled Monday at 00:00 in the account's timezone

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: Some cards are still being rolled out — an empty state isn't an error, it just means the feature has no data yet
Completion rate is a read-only metric; for detailed analysis go to the History section or open a specific test's detail
To change profile settings go to the Profile section; no personal data is edited here

tests.title: About the My tests section
tests.lead: The library of every test you've created or that's been shared with you. This is where you filter them, open them for editing, share them with respondents and see their status (draft, published, archived).

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Create a new test ("New test" button)
Search by name, filter by status and branch
Open a test's detail — edit questions, settings, sharing, password protection
Archive or delete tests you no longer need

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: A new test appears in the list immediately
A published test is available to respondents via the share link within seconds
An archived test remains available in the session history (respondent data isn't lost)

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: Deleting a test is irreversible and also deletes all respondent answers
A password protects entry to the test — it doesn't affect the visibility of results you have access to as the author
You only see tests you own or that have been explicitly shared with you (RLS)

links.label: How to create and publish a test

edu_tests.title: About the Edu tests section
edu_tests.lead: Your educational tests created in Edu mode (typically for schools and courses) — without respondent registration. Here you see every edu test you've created anonymously and then linked to your account using the author password.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Link anonymously created edu tests to your account (by entering the author password on the results page)
Open a linked test's results — score distribution, list of respondents, exports
Track the respondent count in real time
Download results as CSV, JSON or PDF

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Linking a test to your account happens immediately after the correct author password is entered
New respondent sessions appear after refreshing the results page
PDF export is generated directly in the browser (~500 KB library on first use)

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: Without the author password an anonymous edu test cannot be linked to an account — without it the test remains publicly available only via the original share link
Linking doesn't change existing permissions — it only makes access from the main app menu easier
Deleting an edu test also deletes all respondent sessions; the operation is irreversible

links.label: Edu mode: how to create a test without registration
Linking an anonymous test to your account

templates.title: About the Templates section
templates.lead: Ready-made test templates that get you started in seconds — instead of building from scratch. Open them, take a look, and hit "Use" to jump straight into the new-test wizard with pre-filled questions.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Search templates by name
Filter by GDPR purpose (categories derived from the gdpr_purpose field)
Click "Use" to jump into the new-test wizard with the selected template preloaded

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Templates are managed centrally (by the admin team); you don't create or edit them
"Use template" opens the wizard instantly; the test itself is created only after the wizard finishes
If the database has no templates, instead of an empty list you'll see a "Create a test from scratch" prompt

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: Template preview is still on hold — you'll only see metadata, not the actual questions, before using it
Using a template creates a copy — changes to your test in no way affect the original template
The GDPR purpose filter works on an exact value; templates without a purpose set won't appear in any category

library.title: About the Question library section
library.lead: A shared question library available to your team — search, filter, browse. Questions from here go into tests via the question editor inside a test's detail. This is a view only, not an editor.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Search by question text (substring, case-insensitive)
Filter by category or difficulty (easy / medium / hard)
See the question type (single choice, multiple choice, NPS, matrix, …)
The library is read-only — for edits go to a test's detail or to the admin interface (admin)

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Filtering and search are instant (client-side)
The library shows max 60 questions at a time; pagination isn't implemented yet
New questions added in admin appear after refreshing the page

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: The "type" and "category" fields display data from the mock-store; in production they may be empty until schema additions land (AH-12)
The 60-question limit is hardcoded — with a large library you'll only see the first 60
The library shows questions from every author on your team; not just yours

links.label: How to insert questions from the library into a test

audiences.title: About the Audiences section
audiences.lead: Named groups of respondents (e.g. "Q2 Beta testers", "School staff") that make test distribution easier. Here you create groups, rename them, tag them and delete them.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Create a new group (name + optional tags)
Edit the name and tags of an existing group
Delete groups you no longer need (with a confirmation dialog)
See the member count in each group as a badge

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Creating / editing / deleting a group: immediately after confirmation
Email import isn't implemented yet — the button is disabled
Tags are free text without a taxonomy — build your own naming convention

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: You only see groups you created yourself (RLS scoped to owner_id)
Deleting a group doesn't remove the respondents themselves — it only removes the association
Email list import will arrive in a later phase; for now you add respondents manually via a test's share link

history.title: About the History section
history.lead: A reverse-chronological timeline of every event across your tests — respondent sessions, published versions, status changes. It serves as an audit trail and a quick way to orient yourself in activity.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Filter by a specific test (or "All tests")
Filter by event type: Session / Version / Status
Filter by date range (from / to)
Clear all filters with a single click

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: The timeline shows max 100 events at a time — older records aren't accessible via pagination
New respondent sessions appear after refreshing the page
Filters are instant (client-side); no extra network call

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: You only see events from your tests and tests shared with you (RLS); team events from other authors are not visible
The 100-row limit is hardcoded; with high activity, export older events manually for now
Timestamps are rendered in the Slovak locale (sk-SK), regardless of the UI language you've selected

notifications.title: About the Notifications section
notifications.lead: System alerts about activity on your tests — new respondents, milestones reached, anomalies, expirations and daily summaries. Here you read them and mark them as read.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Browse all notifications (read and unread) sorted newest first
Toggle the "Unread only" filter
Mark a single notification as read (click the row)
Mark all unread as read (button above the list — hidden when count is zero)

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Notifications are generated by the server (cron or webhook); refresh for fresh notifications
Marking as read is instant; the unread count badge in the sidebar updates immediately
Notifications stay in the database permanently — no automatic archival

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: Marking a notification as read is irreversible — it can't be set back to "unread"
Notification types (new respondent, milestone, anomaly, expiration, daily summary) are hardcoded; new types from the server render with a fallback colour until we update the UI
You only see notifications for your tests and your account (RLS scope)

links.label: Notification types and when you receive them

teams.title: About the Teams section
teams.lead: Invite and manage team members — create collaborative workspaces with role-based access (owner / editor / viewer). Here you see every team you're a member of and manage who's on each one.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Pick the active team from the cards (the first team is auto-selected on load)
Invite a member: enter an email, pick a role, click "Invite"
Change an existing member's role via the dropdown
Remove a member with the delete button

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Invitations, role changes and removals are all instant
Email invites aren't wired up yet — the "email" field is a placeholder for the AH-12 schema for now
Role changes don't use optimistic UI — the list refetches after success

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: You need a sufficient role (owner) to invite and manage members — the server enforces RLS
Until email invitations ship (AH-12), invited members have to sign in manually and the backend creates the association
You can't delete a team from the UI — that's done by the admin team via support

profile.title: About the Profile section
profile.lead: Your personal settings — name, email, avatar initials, profile handle for public sharing. Here you change the identity that other team members and respondents of shared tests see.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Change your display name (2 – 80 characters)
Change your email (validated, max 255 characters; careful — it can affect sign-in)
Change your avatar initials (1 – 3 alphanumeric characters, auto-uppercase)
Add/change your share handle for the public profile (2 – 32 characters, optional)
Export your personal data (GDPR Art. 15 / 20)
Shortcuts to Security (password + 2FA) and GDPR requests

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: Profile save: instant server mutation + success toast
Avatar initials preview: updates as you type (client-side)
Email change: depends on the auth provider — sometimes requires a verification email at the new address
Data export: kicks off an async job, you'll receive the result by email (typically within hours)

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: Changing your email can break sign-in if the auth provider uses email as the primary identifier — check how yours is set up before saving
Initials are auto-generated once from your name; further name changes don't update them automatically
The share handle is publicly visible — don't use your email or any sensitive data

links.label: GDPR: your rights as a data subject

help.title: About the Help section
help.lead: Help centre — frequently asked questions (FAQ), quick links to legal documents and a button to contact support. Here you look for answers before reaching out to people.

what_you_configure.heading: What you do here
items: Search the FAQ by question or answer text
Expand individual FAQ items (collapsible accordion)
Click quick links: Privacy, Cookies, Changelog, For schools
Contact support by email (mailto link to support@subenai.sk)

time_impact.heading: How quickly changes show up
items: FAQ content is static (i18n bundles, build-time); changes require a deploy
Search and filter are instant (client-side)
Support typically replies within 1 business day (excluding weekends and holidays)

pitfalls.heading: What to watch out for
items: The FAQ doesn't cover every scenario — for a specific question contact support directly
An empty "no results" state means the search found nothing, not that the FAQ is empty
The mailto link opens your default email client; in a browser that may be Gmail/Outlook web depending on your OS settings
